name: typed-stub-semantics
title: Compile-against-stub semantics for typed languages
interface: A specification (and a worked TypeScript or Rust example) of how a contract's interface is materialized as a compilable stub, so an implementation of a parent type-checks against child contracts before any child is implemented — the analogue of proving against sorry-stubbed statements.
nl_description: OPEN. In v0.1 acceptance tests are the only gate; typed stubs would add a compile-time gate and make decomposition cheaper to validate. Includes how stubs are generated from the contract interface and pinned per env.
